knownIssues: Evidence matrix covers only 5 of 30 action x evidence-pair cells (30 = 3 actions x 10 pairs), so most main answers cannot be scored (422 after locking the main call).
Alive counts and the bomb carrier are not stated in the brief.
The brief says the second CT was last seen rotating 30 s ago, which contradicts the follow-up and reveal ("just arrived", "still repositioning").
Only one smoke remains for the entry pair, but the intended best line assumes a smoke on CT and the follow-up assumes it continues.
Distractors are weak: only one line scores 90 or above, so the decision is not a real dilemma.
The best follow-up answer (split_entry) is contestable tactically.
No fact is marked inferred or unknown, so the brief presents nothing as uncertain.
Previously labelled "professional" without any provenance; relabelled synthetic.

brief.title: Banana pressure
brief.focus: Map control and utility management on Inferno

facts.text: Your team holds banana after an early molotov and HE grenade forced the CTs back to site.
The CT anchor used one smoke to delay the push — it has now faded.
A second CT was last seen rotating from A through CT spawn thirty seconds ago.
Your entry pair has one smoke and two flashes remaining.
Forty-five seconds remain in the round.

actions.label: Fake B and rotate to A
Hold banana and wait for information

qualifiers.label: Smoking CT spawn to cut the rotation
Burning all remaining utility on the fake

followup.heading: New sound cue
followup.stimulus: A step sound is heard near coffins — the second CT has arrived at B site.

updates.text: A second defender has been heard at coffins on B site.

responses.label: Continue the B execute with the smoke
Split the entry — one player through construction, one through banana
Abort and rotate to A immediately

events.action: The entry pair smoked CT spawn and split through banana and construction.
events.consequence: The double entry caught the second CT still repositioning after arriving at coffins.
events.state: Both CTs were eliminated. The bomb was planted with twenty-eight seconds remaining.

comparison.roundAction: Split entry onto B site with the CT smoke.
comparison.materialInformation: The sound cue confirming the second CT had arrived at coffins — still repositioning, not yet set up.
comparison.roundFollowup: Splitting the entry exploited the brief window before both CTs were anchored.

debrief.whyItWorks: The CT rotation sound revealed that the second defender had only just arrived and was not yet positioned. A split entry from two angles catches an unset defence.
debrief.cost: Splitting the team reduces trade potential if the first entry dies before the second arrives.
debrief.assumption: The CT heard at coffins has not yet reached a strong post-plant position.
debrief.breaksWhen: If the CT arrived early and is already set up at headshot or dark, the split loses its timing advantage.

evidenceReview.explanation: The CT anchor had already used their smoke, leaving no fast way to delay the execute.
The rotation sound was recent, meaning the second CT was still moving into position — a narrow timing window.

debrief.followupReview: Splitting the entry was the strongest response because it attacked the moment of vulnerability — the period between the second CT arriving and settling into an anchored position.
debrief.strongestAlternative: Proceeding with a standard execute through banana alone. Simpler, maintains trade spacing, but gives both CTs time to cross-fire from set positions.

counterfactual.changedFact: If the second CT had arrived thirty seconds earlier and was already set up at headshot.
counterfactual.effect: A split would walk into a prepared cross-fire. The standard banana execute with a CT smoke would then be safer because it removes the cross-fire angle.

debrief.method: Synthetic scenario written for Roundcraft as editorial tactical analysis. It is not a recording or reconstruction of a professional match.

sources.label: Roundcraft editorial analysis
sources.detail: Synthetic scenario; no professional match, team or player is depicted.

reveal.principle: When a sound cue reveals that a rotating defender is still repositioning, exploit the timing gap before the defence sets — but only if your utility can remove one angle of the cross-fire.
